At compile time, checked word for word by the message tests of `test/messages` with clang:

[cols="1,1,5,2",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Checked on |Message |Fix

|`+aes_on_bearssl+`
|native, wasip2
a|

[listing]
----
webcpp::crypto: ciphers::aes256<backends::bearssl>: BearSSL exports AES only inside its modes, with no block cipher. Name a backend that exports it, as in ciphers::aes256<backends::ctaes> or ciphers::aes256<backends::openssl>, and add its library to the program's Jamfile.
----
|Name ciphers::aes256<backends::ctaes>, include <webcpp/crypto/backends/ctaes.hpp> and add /third_party//ctaes.

|`+bearssl_not_linked+`
|native, wasip2
a|

[listing]
----
webcpp::crypto: the backend BearSSL is used and not linked. In the program's Jamfile, add /third_party//bearssl beside /webcpp/crypto//crypto, or, with /webcpp/crypto//openssl linked, select OpenSSL with <define>WEBCPP_CRYPTO_DEFAULT_BACKEND_OPENSSL. (without b2: define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_BEARSSL=1 and link BearSSL built with webcpp's src/canary_bearssl.c)
----
|Add /third_party//bearssl, or, with OpenSSL linked, define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_DEFAULT_BACKEND_OPENSSL.

|`+ctaes_not_linked+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
a|

[listing]
----
webcpp::crypto: the backend ctaes is used and not linked. In the program's Jamfile, add /third_party//ctaes beside /webcpp/crypto//crypto. (without b2: define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_CTAES=1 and link ctaes.c with webcpp's src/canary_ctaes.c)
----
|Add /third_party//ctaes.

|`+gcm_on_ctaes+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3
a|

[listing]
----
webcpp::crypto: ciphers::gcm<ciphers::aes256<backends::ctaes>>: ctaes exports the AES block cipher alone, and webcpp builds no GCM on another library's AES. Use a backend that exports GCM: ciphers::gcm<ciphers::aes256<backends::bearssl>> or ciphers::gcm<ciphers::aes256<backends::openssl>>.
----
|Use aes256_gcm with BearSSL or OpenSSL linked.

|`+no_backend_native+`
|native
a|

[listing]
----
webcpp::crypto: no backend is linked. In the program's Jamfile, add /webcpp/crypto//openssl (OpenSSL built from source) or /third_party//bearssl (built from source) beside /webcpp/crypto//crypto, as in: exe app : app.cpp /webcpp/crypto//crypto /webcpp/crypto//openssl ; (without b2: define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_OPENSSL=1 and link libcrypto, or define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_BEARSSL=1 and link BearSSL built with webcpp's src/canary_bearssl.c)
----
|Add /webcpp/crypto//openssl or /third_party//bearssl to the program's sources.

|`+no_backend_wasm+`
|wasip2, wasip3
a|

[listing]
----
webcpp::crypto: no backend is linked. On WebAssembly the backend is BearSSL: in the program's Jamfile, add /third_party//bearssl beside /webcpp/crypto//crypto, as in: exe app : app.cpp /webcpp/crypto//crypto /third_party//bearssl ; (without b2: define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_BEARSSL=1 and link BearSSL built with webcpp's src/canary_bearssl.c)
----
|Add /third_party//bearssl to the program's sources.

|`+openssl_not_linked+`
|native, wasip2
a|

[listing]
----
webcpp::crypto: the backend OpenSSL is used and not linked. In the program's Jamfile, add /webcpp/crypto//openssl beside /webcpp/crypto//crypto. (without b2: define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_OPENSSL=1 and link libcrypto)
----
|Add /webcpp/crypto//openssl.

|`+openssl_old+`
|native, wasip2
a|

[listing]
----
webcpp::crypto: the backend OpenSSL needs OpenSSL 3.0 or later, and the headers found are of an older OpenSSL. In the program's Jamfile, name /webcpp/crypto//openssl, which builds OpenSSL 3.5.9. (without b2: put OpenSSL 3's include/ first)
----
|Name /webcpp/crypto//openssl, which builds OpenSSL 3.5.9; without b2, put OpenSSL 3's include/ first.

|`+openssl_only_on_wasi+`
|wasip2, wasip3
a|

[listing]
----
webcpp::crypto: the backend BearSSL is used and not linked. In the program's Jamfile, add /third_party//bearssl beside /webcpp/crypto//crypto, or, with /webcpp/crypto//openssl linked, select OpenSSL with <define>WEBCPP_CRYPTO_DEFAULT_BACKEND_OPENSSL. (without b2: define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_BEARSSL=1 and link BearSSL built with webcpp's src/canary_bearssl.c)
----
|On WASI the default is BearSSL: add /third_party//bearssl, or define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_DEFAULT_BACKEND_OPENSSL.

|`+secp256k1_not_linked+`
|native, wasip2
a|

[listing]
----
webcpp::crypto: <webcpp/crypto/curves/secp256k1.hpp> needs libsecp256k1, which is not linked. In the program's Jamfile, add /third_party//secp256k1 beside /webcpp/crypto//crypto. (without b2: define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_SECP256K1=1 and link libsecp256k1 built with webcpp's src/canary_secp256k1.c)
----
|Add /third_party//secp256k1.

|`+two_defaults+`
|native
a|

[listing]
----
webcpp::crypto: both WEBCPP_CRYPTO_DEFAULT_BACKEND_OPENSSL and WEBCPP_CRYPTO_DEFAULT_BACKEND_BEARSSL are defined. Keep one.
----
|Keep one of the two defines.
|===

|`+default_openssl_on_emscripten+`: OpenSSL selected as the default in a build for Emscripten.
a|

[source,bash]
----
exe app : app.cpp /webcpp/crypto//crypto : <define>WEBCPP_CRYPTO_DEFAULT_BACKEND_OPENSSL ;
----
a|

[listing]
----
all: webcpp::crypto: WEBCPP_CRYPTO_DEFAULT_BACKEND_OPENSSL selects OpenSSL, which is not built for Emscripten. Remove that define, or make it WEBCPP_CRYPTO_DEFAULT_BACKEND_BEARSSL.
----
|Remove the define, or make it WEBCPP_CRYPTO_DEFAULT_BACKEND_BEARSSL.

|`+has_openssl_on_emscripten+`: OpenSSL declared linked, without b2, in a build for Emscripten.
a|

[source,bash]
----
exe app : app.cpp /webcpp/crypto//crypto : <define>WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_OPENSSL=1 ;
----
a|

[listing]
----
all: webcpp::crypto: OpenSSL is not built for Emscripten. In the program's Jamfile, replace /webcpp/crypto//openssl with /third_party//bearssl.
----
|Replace /webcpp/crypto//openssl with /third_party//bearssl.

|`+openssl_on_emscripten+`: /webcpp/crypto//openssl named in a build for Emscripten.
a|

[source,bash]
----
exe app : app.cpp /webcpp/crypto//crypto /webcpp/crypto//openssl ;
----
a|

[listing]
----
all: webcpp::crypto: /webcpp/crypto//openssl is named in a build for Emscripten, where webcpp does not build OpenSSL.
----
|Name /third_party//bearssl in its place for the Emscripten build.

On MSVC, each case of `test/msvc` is proven to stop the build, at compile or at link time; its text is MSVC's own, the same instruction in MSVC's words, and two files compiled with different settings stop the link with LNK2038.

[cols="1,1,4",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Stops |Fix

|`+aes_on_bearssl+`
|the compile
|Name ciphers::aes256<backends::ctaes>, include <webcpp/crypto/backends/ctaes.hpp> and add /third_party//ctaes.

|`+bearssl_not_linked+`
|the compile
|Add /third_party//bearssl, or, with OpenSSL linked, define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_DEFAULT_BACKEND_OPENSSL.

|`+canary_ctaes_missing+`
|the link
|Link /third_party//ctaes.

|`+canary_missing+`
|the link
|Link the library through b2, /third_party//bearssl; built by other means, it must be the pinned commit, with webcpp's src/canary_bearssl.c.

|`+canary_other_commit+`
|the link
|Build the library at the commit of webcpp's submodule, or link it through b2.

|`+canary_other_configuration+`
|the link
|Build BearSSL in webcpp's configuration (getentropy), or link it through b2.

|`+canary_secp256k1_missing+`
|the link
|Link /third_party//secp256k1.

|`+canary_secp256k1_small+`
|the link
|Give the program and the library the same <webcpp-secp256k1-tables>, or link through b2.

|`+canary_two_files+`
|the link
|Compile every file of the program with the same backend settings.

|`+default_two_files+`
|the link
|Give WEBCPP_CRYPTO_DEFAULT_BACKEND_* in the requirements of the program's project, so that every file gets it.

|`+gcm_on_ctaes+`
|the compile
|Use aes256_gcm with BearSSL or OpenSSL linked.

|`+no_backend+`
|the compile
|As no_backend_native.

|`+openssl_not_linked+`
|the compile
|Add /webcpp/crypto//openssl.

|`+two_defaults+`
|the compile
|Keep one of the two defines.
|===
